node.title: Re^4: use of Backticks to catch console output
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
From [https://metacpan.org/dist/IPC-System-Simple/source/lib/IPC/System/Simple.pm|source], ...

You need to trace the source a little further and look into _win32_capture, where you'll see that [mod://Win32::ShellQuote] gets called no matter what the value of $use_shell is.

Both are still very clear that capturex() does not invoke the shell.

In my [id://1180578|experience] the documentation of such modules is usually tailored to *NIX. Either that or people eqate using [mod://Win32::ShellQuote] to "avoiding the shell"*, which isn't quite accurate, and the module does have some edge cases that means it's not the same as [man://execvp] on *NIX - like I said, I was being nitpicky :-)

Have a look at [id://1199200] for more details on calling commands on Windows and why argument quoting is such an issue there.

* Update: See my clarification further down in the thread.
